dialog.description: PatchMan reads issues, acceptance criteria and search results through this connection. It never changes anything in Jira.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.urlHelp: The address you open Jira at. A pasted issue or board link is cut back to the site.
dialog.cloudDesc: Atlassian-hosted (…atlassian.net): your email + an API token.
dialog.datacenterDesc: Self-hosted Jira Server / Data Center: a personal access token.
dialog.cloudHelp: Create an API token in your Atlassian account settings under Security → API tokens. PatchMan reads Jira as you.
dialog.patHelp: Create a personal access token in Jira under your profile → Personal access tokens. PatchMan reads Jira as you.
dialog.backendLocalDesc: The desktop app connects to Jira from your machine.
dialog.backendRemoteDesc: The shared PatchMan server connects; works in the web app too.
dialog.backendNote: The connection is saved to both; this picks which one makes the calls.
dialog.flavorWarning: This site reports itself as "{{type}}": check that the Jira type above is right.
dialog.fieldsFailed: Could not load the Jira fields.
dialog.acFieldHelp: The custom field your team writes acceptance criteria in. Agents and the QA Hub read it as text.
dialog.acFieldNone: None picked: acceptance criteria are read from the description only.
dialog.acFieldAfterTest: Run Test to pick it from this site's fields.
dialog.noCustomFields: This Jira user sees no custom fields.
dialog.defaultJqlPlaceholder: project = ABC AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated DESC
dialog.defaultJqlHelp: Used when a search gives no JQL.

share.title: Share "{{name}}"
share.description: Let people or teams read Jira issues through this connection.
share.identityWarning: People you share with read Jira as this connection's account and see the same projects — the token itself is never shown to them.

panel.title: Jira connections
panel.hint: Each connection reads Jira with its owner's own token. The QA Hub and AI agents (jira_search, jira_issue) use them to read issues and acceptance criteria.
panel.deleteBody: The connection and its shares are removed. Nothing changes in Jira.
